solution:
A line parallel to the X-axis has equation \(y = k\), and \(|k|\) is its distance from the X-axis. Here that distance is 5 and the line lies above the X-axis, so \(k = +5\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y = 5\).

A line parallel to the Y-axis has equation \(x = k\), and \(|k|\) is its distance from the Y-axis. Here that distance is 5 and the line lies to the left of the Y-axis, so \(k = -5\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x = -5\).

Let the required line be \(y = k\), since it is parallel to the X-axis.
Its distance from the point \((-2,\ 3)\) is the vertical distance \(|k - 3|\).
Given \(|k - 3| = 4\), so \(k - 3 = 4\) or \(k - 3 = -4\), giving \(k = 7\) or \(k = -1\).
\(\therefore\) the equation is \(y = 7\) or \(y = -1\).

A line parallel to the X-axis has equation \(y = k\). Its Y-intercept is 3, so it passes through \((0,\ 3)\) and hence \(k = 3\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y = 3\).

A line parallel to the Y-axis has equation \(x = k\). Its X-intercept is 4, so it passes through \((4,\ 0)\) and hence \(k = 4\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x = 4\).

A line parallel to the Y-axis has equation \(x = k\). It contains \(A(2,\ -3)\), so \(k = 2\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x = 2\).

A line parallel to the X-axis has equation \(y = k\). It contains \(B(4,\ -3)\), so \(k = -3\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y = -3\).

Slope of AB \(= \dfrac{4 - 0}{3 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{1} = 4\).
Using the point-slope form at \(A(2,\ 0)\): \(y - 0 = 4(x - 2)\), so \(y = 4x - 8\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(4x - y - 8 = 0\).

\(P(2,\ 1)\) and \(Q(2,\ -1)\) have the same X-co-ordinate, so PQ is parallel to the Y-axis and its slope is not defined.
Every point of the line has \(x = 2\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x = 2\).

Inclination \(\theta = 60^\circ\), so the slope is \(m = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\).
The line passes through the origin, so its equation is \(y = mx\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y = \sqrt{3}\,x\).

Slope of AB \(= \dfrac{7 - 4}{1 - 2} = \dfrac{3}{-1} = -3\).
The required line is parallel to AB, so it has the same slope \(m = -3\), and it passes through the origin, so \(y = mx\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y = -3x\), i.e. \(3x + y = 0\).

Using the point-slope form with \(m = \dfrac{1}{2}\) at the point \((3,\ -2)\):
\(y - (-2) = \dfrac{1}{2}(x - 3)\), so \(2(y + 2) = x - 3\), i.e. \(2y + 4 = x - 3\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x - 2y - 7 = 0\).

Using the point-slope form with \(m = \dfrac{2}{3}\) at \(A(3,\ 5)\):
\(y - 5 = \dfrac{2}{3}(x - 3)\), so \(3(y - 5) = 2(x - 3)\), i.e. \(3y - 15 = 2x - 6\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(2x - 3y + 9 = 0\).

Inclination \(\theta = 120^\circ\), so \(m = \tan 120^\circ = -\tan 60^\circ = -\sqrt{3}\).
Using the point-slope form at \(A(4,\ 3)\): \(y - 3 = -\sqrt{3}(x - 4)\), so \(y - 3 = -\sqrt{3}\,x + 4\sqrt{3}\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(\sqrt{3}\,x + y - 4\sqrt{3} - 3 = 0\).

The line \(3x + y = 6\) meets the X-axis where \(y = 0\), giving \(x = 2\), i.e. at \(A(2,\ 0)\); it meets the Y-axis where \(x = 0\), giving \(y = 6\), i.e. at \(B(0,\ 6)\).
Midpoint of AB \(= \left(\dfrac{2 + 0}{2},\ \dfrac{0 + 6}{2}\right) = (1,\ 3)\).
The required line joins the origin to \((1,\ 3)\), so its slope is \(\dfrac{3 - 0}{1 - 0} = 3\) and \(y = 3x\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(3x - y = 0\).

Since \(y = mx + c\) passes through \(A(2,\ 1)\) and \(B(3,\ 2)\), its slope is
\(m = \dfrac{2 - 1}{3 - 2} = 1\).
Putting \(A(2,\ 1)\) in \(y = mx + c\): \(1 = 1(2) + c\), so \(c = -1\).
\(\therefore\) \(m = 1\) and \(c = -1\).

Inclination \(135^\circ\) gives slope \(m = \tan 135^\circ = -1\).
X-intercept 7 means the line passes through \((7,\ 0)\).
Point-slope form: \(y - 0 = -1(x - 7)\), so \(y = -x + 7\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x + y - 7 = 0\).

Slope of BC \(= \dfrac{6 - 0}{-1 - 2} = \dfrac{6}{-3} = -2\).
Using the point-slope form at \(B(2,\ 0)\): \(y - 0 = -2(x - 2)\), so \(y = -2x + 4\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of line BC is \(2x + y - 4 = 0\).

D is the midpoint of BC, so \(D = \left(\dfrac{2 + (-1)}{2},\ \dfrac{0 + 6}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2},\ 3\right)\).
Slope of AD \(= \dfrac{3 - 4}{\frac{1}{2} - 3} = \dfrac{-1}{-\frac{5}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{5}\).
Using the point-slope form at \(A(3,\ 4)\): \(y - 4 = \dfrac{2}{5}(x - 3)\), so \(5y - 20 = 2x - 6\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the median AD is \(2x - 5y + 14 = 0\).

Midpoint of AB \(= \left(\dfrac{3 + 2}{2},\ \dfrac{4 + 0}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{2},\ 2\right)\).
Midpoint of BC \(= \left(\dfrac{2 + (-1)}{2},\ \dfrac{0 + 6}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2},\ 3\right)\).
Slope of the line joining them \(= \dfrac{3 - 2}{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{5}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Point-slope form at \(\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\ 3\right)\): \(y - 3 = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\), so \(4y - 12 = -2x + 1\).
\(\therefore\) the required equation is \(2x + 4y - 13 = 0\).

The equation is already in the intercept form \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\), with \(a = 3\) and \(b = 2\).
\(\therefore\) X-intercept \(= 3\) and Y-intercept \(= 2\).

Write the equation in the intercept form \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\):
\(\dfrac{3x}{2} + \dfrac{2y}{3} = 1\) becomes \(\dfrac{x}{\frac{2}{3}} + \dfrac{y}{\frac{3}{2}} = 1\).
\(\therefore\) X-intercept \(= \dfrac{2}{3}\) and Y-intercept \(= \dfrac{3}{2}\).

\(2x - 3y + 12 = 0\) gives \(2x - 3y = -12\). Dividing throughout by \(-12\):
\(\dfrac{x}{-6} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1\).
\(\therefore\) X-intercept \(= -6\) and Y-intercept \(= 4\).

Case 1: the line has non-zero intercepts \(a\) and \(b\) with \(a + b = 0\), so \(b = -a\).
Its equation \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{-a} = 1\) becomes \(x - y = a\). Putting \(A(1,\ 3)\): \(1 - 3 = a\), so \(a = -2\) and the line is \(x - y + 2 = 0\).
Case 2: both intercepts are 0 (their sum is then also 0), so the line passes through the origin, \(y = mx\). Putting \(A(1,\ 3)\): \(3 = m\), so the line is \(3x - y = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the required lines are \(x - y + 2 = 0\) and \(3x - y = 0\).

Case 1: equal non-zero intercepts \(a\). Then \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{a} = 1\), i.e. \(x + y = a\). Putting \(A(3,\ 4)\): \(3 + 4 = a\), so \(a = 7\) and the line is \(x + y = 7\).
Case 2: both intercepts equal 0, so the line passes through the origin, \(y = mx\). Putting \(A(3,\ 4)\): \(4 = 3m\), so \(m = \dfrac{4}{3}\) and the line is \(4x - 3y = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the required lines are \(x + y = 7\) and \(4x - 3y = 0\).

An altitude through a vertex is perpendicular to the opposite side.
Altitude from A: slope of BC \(= \dfrac{-3 - (-1)}{-4 - 6} = \dfrac{-2}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}\), so the altitude has slope \(-5\). At \(A(2,\ 5)\): \(y - 5 = -5(x - 2)\), giving \(5x + y - 15 = 0\).
Altitude from B: slope of AC \(= \dfrac{-3 - 5}{-4 - 2} = \dfrac{-8}{-6} = \dfrac{4}{3}\), so the altitude has slope \(-\dfrac{3}{4}\). At \(B(6,\ -1)\): \(4(y + 1) = -3(x - 6)\), giving \(3x + 4y - 14 = 0\).
Altitude from C: slope of AB \(= \dfrac{-1 - 5}{6 - 2} = \dfrac{-6}{4} = -\dfrac{3}{2}\), so the altitude has slope \(\dfrac{2}{3}\). At \(C(-4,\ -3)\): \(3(y + 3) = 2(x + 4)\), giving \(2x - 3y - 1 = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the altitudes are \(5x + y - 15 = 0\), \(3x + 4y - 14 = 0\) and \(2x - 3y - 1 = 0\).

The perpendicular bisector of a side passes through its midpoint and is perpendicular to it.
Side PQ: midpoint \(\left(\dfrac{-1 + 4}{2},\ \dfrac{8 - 2}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2},\ 3\right)\); slope of PQ \(= \dfrac{-2 - 8}{4 + 1} = -2\), so the bisector has slope \(\dfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(y - 3 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\), i.e. \(4y - 12 = 2x - 3\), giving \(2x - 4y + 9 = 0\).
Side QR: midpoint \(\left(\dfrac{4 - 5}{2},\ \dfrac{-2 - 3}{2}\right) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\ -\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\); slope of QR \(= \dfrac{-3 + 2}{-5 - 4} = \dfrac{1}{9}\), so the bisector has slope \(-9\). Then \(y + \dfrac{5}{2} = -9\left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\), giving \(9x + y + 7 = 0\).
Side PR: midpoint \(\left(\dfrac{-1 - 5}{2},\ \dfrac{8 - 3}{2}\right) = \left(-3,\ \dfrac{5}{2}\right)\); slope of PR \(= \dfrac{-3 - 8}{-5 + 1} = \dfrac{11}{4}\), so the bisector has slope \(-\dfrac{4}{11}\). Then \(11\left(y - \dfrac{5}{2}\right) = -4(x + 3)\), i.e. \(11y - \dfrac{55}{2} = -4x - 12\), giving \(8x + 22y - 31 = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the perpendicular bisectors are \(2x - 4y + 9 = 0\), \(9x + y + 7 = 0\) and \(8x + 22y - 31 = 0\).

The orthocenter is the point of intersection of any two altitudes.
Altitude from A: slope of BC \(= \dfrac{0 - 1}{-1 - 1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so this altitude has slope \(-2\). At \(A(2,\ -2)\): \(y + 2 = -2(x - 2)\), giving \(2x + y - 2 = 0\).
Altitude from B: slope of AC \(= \dfrac{0 + 2}{-1 - 2} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\), so this altitude has slope \(\dfrac{3}{2}\). At \(B(1,\ 1)\): \(2(y - 1) = 3(x - 1)\), giving \(3x - 2y - 1 = 0\).
Solving: from the first, \(y = 2 - 2x\); substituting, \(3x - 2(2 - 2x) - 1 = 0\), so \(7x = 5\), \(x = \dfrac{5}{7}\) and \(y = 2 - \dfrac{10}{7} = \dfrac{4}{7}\).
\(\therefore\) the orthocenter is \(\left(\dfrac{5}{7},\ \dfrac{4}{7}\right)\).

Slope of ON, where \(O(0,\ 0)\) and \(N(3,\ -4)\), is \(\dfrac{-4 - 0}{3 - 0} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\).
Since ON \(\perp\) L, slope of L \(= -\dfrac{1}{-\frac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{4}\).
Line L passes through \(N(3,\ -4)\): \(y + 4 = \dfrac{3}{4}(x - 3)\), so \(4y + 16 = 3x - 9\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of line L is \(3x - 4y = 25\).

Write \(2x + 3y - 6 = 0\) as \(y = -\dfrac{2}{3}x + 2\), which is the slope-intercept form.
So slope \(m = -\dfrac{2}{3}\) and Y-intercept \(= 2\).
For the X-intercept put \(y = 0\): \(2x - 6 = 0\), so \(x = 3\).
\(\therefore\) slope \(= -\dfrac{2}{3}\), X-intercept \(= 3\), Y-intercept \(= 2\).

Write \(3x - y - 9 = 0\) as \(y = 3x - 9\).
So slope \(m = 3\) and Y-intercept \(= -9\).
For the X-intercept put \(y = 0\): \(3x - 9 = 0\), so \(x = 3\).
\(\therefore\) slope \(= 3\), X-intercept \(= 3\), Y-intercept \(= -9\).

Write \(x + 2y = 0\) as \(y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x\), so slope \(m = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Putting \(y = 0\) gives \(x = 0\), and putting \(x = 0\) gives \(y = 0\); the line passes through the origin.
\(\therefore\) slope \(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\), X-intercept \(= 0\), Y-intercept \(= 0\).

\(y = 2x - 4\). Shifting every term to one side, \(2x - y - 4 = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the required form is \(2x - y - 4 = 0\).

\(y = 4\), i.e. \(y - 4 = 0\). Writing the missing \(x\) term with coefficient 0,
\(\therefore\) the required form is \(0x + 1y - 4 = 0\).

\(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1\). Multiplying throughout by 4: \(2x + y = 4\).
\(\therefore\) the required form is \(2x + y - 4 = 0\).

\(\dfrac{x}{3} - \dfrac{y}{2} = 0\). Multiplying throughout by 6: \(2x - 3y = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the required form is \(2x - 3y + 0 = 0\).

For a line \(ax + by + c = 0\) the slope is \(-\dfrac{a}{b}\).
Slope of \(x - 2y - 7 = 0\) is \(-\dfrac{1}{-2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
Slope of \(2x - 4y + 15 = 0\) is \(-\dfrac{2}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
The slopes are equal. Also the lines are not the same line, since \(\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{-2}{-4} \ne \dfrac{-7}{15}\).
\(\therefore\) the two lines are parallel to each other.

Slope of \(x - 2y - 7 = 0\) is \(m_1 = -\dfrac{1}{-2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\); slope of \(2x + y + 1 = 0\) is \(m_2 = -\dfrac{2}{1} = -2\).
Since \(m_1 \times m_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (-2) = -1\), the lines are perpendicular to each other.
For their intersection, from \(2x + y + 1 = 0\) we get \(y = -2x - 1\). Substituting in \(x - 2y - 7 = 0\):
\(x - 2(-2x - 1) - 7 = 0\), so \(5x - 5 = 0\), giving \(x = 1\) and \(y = -3\).
\(\therefore\) the lines are perpendicular and their point of intersection is \((1,\ -3)\).

Putting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = p\) gives the X-intercept \(\dfrac{p}{3}\); putting \(x = 0\) gives the Y-intercept \(\dfrac{p}{4}\).
The triangle formed with the axes is right-angled at the origin, so its area is
\(\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\dfrac{p}{3}\right|\left|\dfrac{p}{4}\right| = \dfrac{p^{2}}{24}\).
Given \(\dfrac{p^{2}}{24} = 24\), so \(p^{2} = 576\).
\(\therefore\) \(p = \pm 24\).

Slope of \(3x - y - 1 = 0\) is 3, so the perpendicular from A has slope \(-\dfrac{1}{3}\).
Its equation through \(A(-2,\ 3)\) is \(y - 3 = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x + 2)\), i.e. \(x + 3y - 7 = 0\).
The foot is the intersection of this with \(3x - y - 1 = 0\), i.e. \(y = 3x - 1\):
\(x + 3(3x - 1) - 7 = 0\), so \(10x = 10\), giving \(x = 1\) and \(y = 2\).
\(\therefore\) the foot of the perpendicular is \((1,\ 2)\).

The circumcenter is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides.
Side AC: \(A(-2,\ 3)\) and \(C(4,\ 3)\) have the same Y-co-ordinate, so AC is horizontal with midpoint \((1,\ 3)\); its perpendicular bisector is the vertical line \(x = 1\).
Side AB: midpoint \(\left(\dfrac{-2 + 6}{2},\ \dfrac{3 - 1}{2}\right) = (2,\ 1)\); slope of AB \(= \dfrac{-1 - 3}{6 + 2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\), so its perpendicular bisector has slope 2: \(y - 1 = 2(x - 2)\), i.e. \(y = 2x - 3\).
Putting \(x = 1\) gives \(y = -1\).
\(\therefore\) the circumcenter is \((1,\ -1)\).

Altitude from A: slope of BC \(= \dfrac{2 - 6}{-1 - 7} = \dfrac{-4}{-8} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so this altitude has slope \(-2\). At \(A(3,\ -2)\): \(y + 2 = -2(x - 3)\), i.e. \(2x + y - 4 = 0\).
Altitude from B: slope of AC \(= \dfrac{2 + 2}{-1 - 3} = -1\), so this altitude has slope 1. At \(B(7,\ 6)\): \(y - 6 = 1(x - 7)\), i.e. \(x - y - 1 = 0\).
Solving, \(y = x - 1\) and \(2x + (x - 1) - 4 = 0\) give \(3x = 5\), so \(x = \dfrac{5}{3}\) and \(y = \dfrac{2}{3}\).
\(\therefore\) the orthocenter is \(\left(\dfrac{5}{3},\ \dfrac{2}{3}\right)\).

First find where the first two lines meet. Multiplying \(3x - 4y + 5 = 0\) by 2 gives \(6x - 8y + 10 = 0\); subtracting this from \(7x - 8y + 5 = 0\) gives \(x - 5 = 0\), so \(x = 5\).
Then \(3(5) - 4y + 5 = 0\) gives \(4y = 20\), so \(y = 5\). The first two lines meet at \((5,\ 5)\).
Substituting in the third line: \(4(5) + 5(5) - 45 = 20 + 25 - 45 = 0\), so \((5,\ 5)\) lies on it too.
\(\therefore\) the three lines are concurrent and their point of concurrence is \((5,\ 5)\).

Slope of \(3x - y + 23 = 0\) is 3, so the required line has slope \(-\dfrac{1}{3}\).
Its X-intercept is 3, so it passes through \((3,\ 0)\): \(y - 0 = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x - 3)\), i.e. \(3y = -x + 3\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(x + 3y = 3\).

The distance of \((x_1,\ y_1)\) from \(ax + by + c = 0\) is \(\dfrac{|ax_1 + by_1 + c|}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}\).
For \(O(0,\ 0)\) and \(7x + 24y - 50 = 0\):
distance \(= \dfrac{|7(0) + 24(0) - 50|}{\sqrt{7^{2} + 24^{2}}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{625}} = \dfrac{50}{25}\).
\(\therefore\) the distance of the origin from the line is 2 units.

Using \(\dfrac{|ax_1 + by_1 + c|}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}\) with \(A(-2,\ 3)\) and \(12x - 5y - 13 = 0\):
distance \(= \dfrac{|12(-2) - 5(3) - 13|}{\sqrt{12^{2} + (-5)^{2}}} = \dfrac{|-24 - 15 - 13|}{\sqrt{169}} = \dfrac{52}{13}\).
\(\therefore\) the required distance is 4 units.

The lines \(4x - 3y + 5 = 0\) and \(4x - 3y + 7 = 0\) have the same coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\), so they are parallel.
Distance between parallel lines \(ax + by + c_1 = 0\) and \(ax + by + c_2 = 0\) is \(\dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}\):
distance \(= \dfrac{|5 - 7|}{\sqrt{4^{2} + (-3)^{2}}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{25}} = \dfrac{2}{5}\).
\(\therefore\) the distance between the lines is \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) units.

First make the coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) the same. Multiplying \(3x + 2y + 6 = 0\) by 3 gives \(9x + 6y + 18 = 0\).
Now using \(\dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}\) with \(9x + 6y - 7 = 0\) and \(9x + 6y + 18 = 0\):
distance \(= \dfrac{|-7 - 18|}{\sqrt{9^{2} + 6^{2}}} = \dfrac{25}{\sqrt{117}}\).
\(\therefore\) the distance between the lines is \(\dfrac{25}{\sqrt{117}} = \dfrac{25}{3\sqrt{13}}\) units.

Note first that the two lines named in the printed question, \(x + y - 4 = 0\) and \(x + y - 2 = 0\), are parallel to each other, and every point of the first is at distance \(\dfrac{|-4 + 2|}{\sqrt{1^{2} + 1^{2}}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\) units from the second. So no point can be at distance 1 unit, and the question as printed has no answer. The intended second line is \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\); it is solved below.
Any point on \(x + y - 4 = 0\) can be written as \(P(t,\ 4 - t)\).
Its distance from \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\) is \(\dfrac{|4t + 3(4 - t) - 10|}{\sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2}}} = \dfrac{|t + 2|}{5}\).
Setting this equal to 1: \(|t + 2| = 5\), so \(t = 3\) or \(t = -7\).
\(t = 3\) gives \((3,\ 1)\) and \(t = -7\) gives \((-7,\ 11)\).
\(\therefore\) the required points are \((3,\ 1)\) and \((-7,\ 11)\).
_note: Book stem defect (already adjudicated). As printed the question asks for points on x+y-4=0 at distance 1 from x+y-2=0, but those two lines are PARALLEL: every point of the first is at distance 2/sqrt(2)=sqrt(2) from the second, never 1, so the printed question has no solution. The intended second line is 4x+3y-10=0, which reproduces the printed key (3,1) and (-7,11) exactly. Solved against the intended form, with the defect stated in the solution.

solution:
From \(x + y - 2 = 0\), \(y = 2 - x\). Substituting in \(4x + 3y = 10\):
\(4x + 3(2 - x) = 10\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = -2\). The lines meet at \((4,\ -2)\).
A line parallel to the X-axis has equation \(y = k\); passing through \((4,\ -2)\) gives \(k = -2\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(y + 2 = 0\).

From \(x + y - 2 = 0\), \(y = 2 - x\). Substituting in \(2x - 3y + 4 = 0\):
\(2x - 3(2 - x) + 4 = 0\), so \(5x = 2\), giving \(x = \dfrac{2}{5}\) and \(y = \dfrac{8}{5}\).
The required line joins \(\left(\dfrac{2}{5},\ \dfrac{8}{5}\right)\) to the X-intercept point \((3,\ 0)\); its slope is
\(\dfrac{0 - \frac{8}{5}}{3 - \frac{2}{5}} = \dfrac{-\frac{8}{5}}{\frac{13}{5}} = -\dfrac{8}{13}\).
Through \((3,\ 0)\): \(13y = -8(x - 3)\), i.e. \(13y = -8x + 24\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the line is \(8x + 13y - 24 = 0\).

The bisector of angle BAC at vertex \(A(4,\ 3)\) has the direction of the sum of the unit vectors along AB and AC.
Along AB: \(B - A = (-4,\ -3)\) with \(|AB| = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5\), so the unit vector is \(\left(-\dfrac{4}{5},\ -\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\).
Along AC: \(C - A = (-2,\ 0)\) with \(|AC| = 2\), so the unit vector is \((-1,\ 0)\).
Their sum is \(\left(-\dfrac{9}{5},\ -\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\), which is parallel to \((3,\ 1)\), so the bisector has slope \(\dfrac{1}{3}\).
Through \(A(4,\ 3)\): \(3(y - 3) = 1(x - 4)\), i.e. \(3y - 9 = x - 4\).
\(\therefore\) the equation of the bisector of angle BAC is \(x - 3y + 5 = 0\).

In \(\triangle ABC\) the segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side. So DE \(\parallel\) AB, EF \(\parallel\) BC and DF \(\parallel\) CA.
Side AB passes through \(F(-5,\ -3)\) and is parallel to DE, whose slope is \(\dfrac{-2 - 8}{4 + 1} = -2\). Then \(y + 3 = -2(x + 5)\), i.e. \(2x + y + 13 = 0\).
Side BC passes through \(D(-1,\ 8)\) and is parallel to EF, whose slope is \(\dfrac{-3 + 2}{-5 - 4} = \dfrac{1}{9}\). Then \(9(y - 8) = 1(x + 1)\), i.e. \(x - 9y + 73 = 0\).
Side CA passes through \(E(4,\ -2)\) and is parallel to DF, whose slope is \(\dfrac{-3 - 8}{-5 + 1} = \dfrac{11}{4}\). Then \(4(y + 2) = 11(x - 4)\), i.e. \(11x - 4y - 52 = 0\).
\(\therefore\) the sides of \(\triangle ABC\) are \(2x + y + 13 = 0\), \(x - 9y + 73 = 0\) and \(11x - 4y - 52 = 0\).

The circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC\) is the point equidistant from A, B, C, and since D, E, F are the midpoints of the sides, it is the intersection of the perpendiculars drawn to the sides through those midpoints.
Through \(D(-1,\ 8)\), perpendicular to BC (slope \(\dfrac{1}{9}\)) so slope \(-9\): \(y - 8 = -9(x + 1)\), i.e. \(9x + y + 1 = 0\).
Through \(E(4,\ -2)\), perpendicular to CA (slope \(\dfrac{11}{4}\)) so slope \(-\dfrac{4}{11}\): \(11(y + 2) = -4(x - 4)\), i.e. \(4x + 11y + 6 = 0\).

Side opposite \(O\) is \(AB = 10\), opposite \(A\) is \(OB = 8\), opposite \(B\) is \(OA = 6\), and \(10 + 8 + 6 = 24\).
